title: Credit Analyst
description:
The Credit Analyst will evaluate financial statements, credit histories, and market data to assess the creditworthiness of corporate and individual clients within the BFSI sector. Working closely with the back‑office team, you will provide actionable insights, ensure compliance with internal policies, and help maintain strong customer relationships through timely and accurate credit decisions.
  

* Conduct detailed credit assessments using financial statements, credit scores, and industry trends.
* Prepare and present credit risk reports for senior management and lending committees.
* Monitor existing credit portfolios for early warning signs and recommend corrective actions.
* Collaborate with Customer Care Executives to address client inquiries related to credit decisions.
* Ensure all credit analyses comply with regulatory standards and internal policies.
* Maintain accurate documentation of credit files and audit trails.
* Assist in the development and refinement of credit scoring models and underwriting guidelines.
* Support the back‑office team in processing loan applications and documentation verification.
* Participate in cross‑functional meetings to improve credit processes and customer experience.
* Stay updated on market developments, regulatory changes, and emerging credit risks.

  

* Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics, Business Administration, or related field.
* 2+ years of experience in credit analysis, underwriting, or risk assessment within BFSI.
* Strong analytical skills with proficiency in Excel and credit analysis software.
* Knowledge of regulatory frameworks such as RBI guidelines and Basel norms.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
* Ability to work independently and as part of a back‑office team.
* Detail‑oriented with strong organizational and documentation skills.
* Customer‑focused mindset with experience handling client inquiries.
* Professional certifications (e.g., CFA, ICAI) are a plus.
* Proficiency in MS Office Suite and familiarity with CRM/ERP systems.

title: Enterprise Risk Management - Senior Analyst
description:
**Description**
---------------

**About Willis Towers Watson**

Willis Towers Watson (NASDAQ: WTW) is a leading global advisory, broking and solutions company that helps clients around the world turn risk into a path for growth. With roots dating to 1828, Willis Towers Watson has 45,000 employees serving more than 140 countries and markets.  
We design and deliver solutions that manage risk, optimize benefits, cultivate talent, and expand the power of capital to protect and strengthen institutions and individuals. Our unique perspective allows us to see the critical intersections between talent, assets, and ideas — the dynamic formula that drives business performance.  
Together, we unlock potential

**About The Team**

The Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) team sits within WTW's Risk function. Its work covers risk identification, assessment, monitoring, reporting and stakeholder engagement.

**About The Role**

The role supports day-to-day Enterprise Risk activities and projects under the guidance of the Enterprise Risk team.

**Role:** Senior Analyst – Enterprise Risk Management (ERM)

**Shift Timings:** Day Shift: 10.30 AM to 7:30 PM.

**Job Location:** Thane

**Job Summary**
===============

Contribute to the effective execution and ongoing improvement of the Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) Framework across assigned segments and geographies, ERM business-as-usual activities and projects.

Apply established ERM procedures and concepts, basic industry knowledge, sound judgment and experience to support risk identification, assessment, monitoring, reporting, analysis and stakeholder engagement under the guidance of the Enterprise Risk team.

Support a consistent risk reporting environment by preparing accurate information, coordinating assigned activities, completing agreed actions and contributing to risk forums and project outcomes.

Provide backup cover for designated team members in areas of the wider Risk function outside ERM, supporting continuity of key activities and deliverables.

  

**Principal Accountabilities**

* Individual contributor role within the Expert career band, with the primary focus on applying ERM knowledge and concepts through own work, thereby completing the assigned activities effectively
* Scope: assigned WTW geography / geographies and segments, ERM BAU / projects and support for broader Risk Function team members (India centre based)
* Contribute to projects and team objectives by applying risk management knowledge, data management, analytical and reporting skills
* Work with guidance from Enterprise Risk team on routine technical challenges, using judgment and experience to recommend practical solutions and escalate complex matters (where required)
* Build positive working relationships, communicate proactively and complete assigned tasks to agreed quality and timelines
* Fulfil responsibilities as assigned

  

**Principal Duties/Responsibilities**

**Key responsibilities**

* Prepare materials, data and action logs for country, segment and line-of-business risk forums; support discussions and document agreed outcomes for assigned geographies/segments
* Review assigned risk registers, validate completeness of risk and control information, and follow up on mitigation actions with Risk Champions / Coordinators and relevant stakeholders
* Prepare accurate and timely risk reports for Business and Function Leaders across assigned geographies/segments.
* Contribute to Enterprise Risk business activities and projects by completing assigned analysis, documentation, coordination and follow-up activities
* Proactively identify areas to evolve reporting, analysis and procedures to enhance value and improve effectiveness and efficiency
* Provide stakeholders with guidance on established policies, controls and framework requirements, referring complex interpretation matters to senior risk colleagues
* Deliver approved basic and advanced risk training materials to Risk Coordinators, with guidance from senior ERM colleagues as appropriate
* Participate in relevant business review meetings, contribute observations and share approved good practices that may help reduce risk
* Maintain reporting and action tracking for Risk Acceptances, Risk Exceptions and related ERM activities
* Maintain a working knowledge of the processes and responsibilities of two designated team members outside ERM and provide backup cover as required, completing agreed activities within established procedures and timelines and escalating issues appropriately.

**Report outcomes**

* Prepare regular updates as part of the Enterprise Risk team on monthly and quarterly business engagements, clearly recording decisions, owners, actions and due dates.
* Summarise actions taken to manage risks, serious or persistent issues, monitoring and sampling results, relevant regulatory, economic or political developments, and other material matters
* Escalate risk matters within the Enterprise Risk team and ensure information is recorded in the appropriate enterprise log, database or tool

**Manage own delivery**

* Create quarterly action plans aligned with annual objectives and report progress, issues and dependencies
* Organise and prioritise assigned work, proactively communicate status and risks to delivery, and seek guidance when matters exceed the role’s authority or experience

**Manage internal relationships**

* Maintain positive working relationships with Business and Function Heads, Risk Champions / Coordinators and colleagues to support effective interaction between risk and the business
* Collaborate across the Risk Function and other related stakeholders, to exchange information and support agreed outcomes
* Contribute to team discussions, knowledge sharing and continuous learning activities

  

**Communications and Relationships**

* ERM colleagues and stakeholders across the assigned geographies and segments

  Risk Function, Risk Champions / Coordinators, Business and Function colleagues

**Competencies**

* Action-oriented and accountable for own deliverables
* Work effectively with stakeholders, including senior leaders, within defined responsibilities
* Collaboration and contribution to team learning
* Organising and prioritising
* Clear written, verbal and presentation communication
* Analytical thinking and sound judgment
* Practical problem solving using established procedures and guidance
* Attention to detail and quality

  Proactive communication and timely escalation

**Required Skills, Knowledge, Experience**

**Skills:**

* Good understanding of ERM procedures and concepts, with the ability to apply them effectively to assigned activities

title: Data Analyst
description:
**About Darkroom**
Darkroom (Darkroom Digital, Inc.) is the leading next-generation growth marketing firm engineering the brands of tomorrow. Founded in 2017, we set out to redefine what a modern agency could be, by replacing the inertia of legacy advertising behemoths with a model built for speed, intelligence, and measurable impact.
  
  
At our core, Darkroom is a human services company powered by Shadow, a universal AI commerce layer that integrates executive-level strategy with proprietary agentic technology. This fusion enables our teams to deliver outsized returns by enhancing creative output, operational efficiency, and revenue generation across every stage of the customer journey.
  
  
Our track record speaks for itself: billions in attributable revenue driven across e-commerce marketplaces, media networks, DTC ecosystems, and social commerce platforms. Every engagement feeds into our proprietary data infrastructure, enabling a continuous feedback loop that accelerates growth, improves margins, and compounds results across our client portfolio.
  
  
What began as a boutique design studio has evolved into one of the fastest-growing private companies in America (Inc. 5000) and among the most effective performance media agencies of the 2020s (Varos). Our founders were recognized by Forbes 30 Under 30 for advancing the intersection of technology, marketing, and advertising, cementing Darkroom’s role as a defining player in the future of media innovation.
  
  
**About The Role**
You'll also own the company metrics our CEO reviews every week: retention, cohorts, media mix and creator spend.
  
  
You'll report to the SVP of Finance, with a dotted line to our Shadow data team, who build the data pipelines you'll work from. You'll work closely with our FP&A Analyst, our department Managing Directors and sales leadership.
  
  
This role is built for someone who sees AI as a core part of how finance gets done. You'll use tools like Claude to build models, automate reporting and create systems that department leaders can use on their own.
  
  
**This is a fully remote role supporting a team in the EST time zone (9 AM–5 PM EST).**
****What You’ll Do****

* In your first 30 days, audit utilization across every department, role and person.
* Build and own the utilization model on both a recurring (MRR) and non-recurring (NRR) revenue basis, including Shadow FTEs, the capacity our AI platform adds.
* Publish weekly utilization reporting by department, and track capacity for each Managing Director.
* Project utilization from the sales pipeline, working with the sales team.
* Build a hiring case for every hiring request: current utilization, pipeline, margin impact and a clear recommendation.
* Own the staffing sheets, open-role placeholders and the staffing ledgers for custom deals.
* Build cohort reporting (retention maps, layer cakes, curves and scorecards) by company, department, leader and client, including a monthly cohort spotlight for department heads.
* Track net revenue retention, logo retention, churn and lifetime value.
* Report on media mix: spend by channel and concentration, spend growth by client, take rate and ROI by channel, platform revenue share, and client-specific spend reporting.
* Analyze creator spend: who we pay and the average price per creator.
* Prepare a weekly metrics report for the CEO covering retention, cohorts, media mix and utilization.
* Define the metrics and data our reports need with the Shadow data team, and keep them consistent with our financial reporting.
* Provide utilization and performance inputs to the FP&A team for the forecast, the annual budget and our incentive plans.
* Build reports, automations and simple systems that department leaders can use themselves.

****You Should Apply If This Sounds Like You****

* You have 2-4 years of experience in data analytics, FP&A, consulting or operations analytics, ideally in a professional services, agency or e-commerce business.
* You have hands-on experience with utilization, capacity or resource planning, and you understand how it drives margin in a services business.
* You're advanced in Google Sheets or Excel and you build models others can follow.
* SQL or Python is a strong plus.
* You understand billable rates, margin and retention metrics, or you can learn them fast.
* You turn data into a clear recommendation, and you can hold your ground with senior leaders using data instead of opinion.
* You enjoy building systems and automations, not just running reports.
* You already use Claude or similar AI tools in your work and can point to real examples.
* You're fluent in written and spoken English.

****What It’s Like to Work at Darkroom****
Darkroom is not a typical agency. We are looking for A players who want to build something great. We move fast, think deeply, and expect every team member to bring insight and rigor to everything they touch. We hold a high bar for performance, creativity, and ownership, but we also support each other relentlessly. No egos, no red tape, just world-class talent building something remarkable.
  
  
We believe in autonomy with accountability, truth over comfort, and outcomes over optics.
  
  

* Unlimited PTO + local holidays (relevant to your hub): Rebooting is part of the work. Take the time you need to stay sharp.
* Remote-First Culture: Many roles are fully remote. Employees based in or near our New York or Lisbon HQs are expected to work hybrid with weekly in-office time. Hub locations include Brazil, Portugal and Spain.
* Parental Leave: Flexible parental leave to support new parents during this important transition.
* Growth: Our interdisciplinary model gives every Darkroomer exposure far beyond their core role. Grow your skills, expand your influence, and stay at the forefront of the industry.

****Equal Opportunity Statement****
Darkroom is an equal opportunity workplace. We are dedicated to equal employment opportunities regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity, or Veteran status. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements.

title: Senior Analyst- FP&A
description: About the Role:Qualicentric embeds senior finance capability inside US mid-market companies and deal teams, delivering the analytical depth of a Big-4 or specialist advisory practice at the economics of an outsourced model. The Senior Analyst sits at the core of this delivery - translating raw client data into the financial models, reports, and diligence workpapers that drive CFO decisions and deal outcomes.Unlike a traditional in-house analyst role, you will work across two complementary mandates. On the ongoing advisory side, you support FP&A and management reporting for clients where Qualicentric acts as an embedded finance function. On the transaction side, you build the analytical workpapers underpinning Quality of Earnings and working capital analyses for live US deal mandates. The skillset is the same; the context shifts by engagement.This is a role for someone who takes pride in the quality of their own work product - who notices when a number does not reconcile, who formats a model so it can be audited, and who asks the right question before building in the wrong direction.WHAT YOU WILL DO1. FP&A & Management Reporting• Build and maintain driver-based financial models: monthly actuals vs. budget variance analysis, rolling forecasts, and scenario analyses under the direction of the Manager• Prepare management reporting deliverables - monthly P&L packs, KPI dashboards, and variance commentary decks - ensuring numbers tie end-to-end across all schedules• Populate and maintain integrated three-statement models (P&L, balance sheet, cash flow) with operating KPI bridges; flag model integrity issues proactively• Maintain 13-week cash flow trackers and covenant compliance schedules with weekly updates coordinated against client accounting data• Support CFO presentation preparation: build charts, tables, and bridge analyses in Excel and PowerPoint to a client-ready standard• Perform ad hoc financial analyses - pricing and margin analyses, department-level cost deep-dives, customer profitability reviews - as directed by the engagement lead2. Financial Due Diligence & Transaction Support• Build and maintain the QoE workbook - populating normalising adjustment schedules, sourcing supporting documents from the data room, and maintaining a clean audit trail for each adjustment• Construct revenue disaggregation analyses: customer-level waterfall schedules, cohort trends, channel mix, and concentration summaries across the trailing analysis period• Build working capital analyses: monthly NWC calculation schedules, seasonality overlays, and peg determination support under the direction of the engagement Manager• Populate net debt schedules - debt instruments, capital lease obligations, deferred revenue, unfunded liabilities - with values sourced directly from client balance sheets and supporting documents• Prepare management information schedules and document request trackers; maintain version control across data room iterations• Draft supporting sections of the FDD report - revenue analysis, working capital commentary, net debt schedule - with clear sourcing, defined adjustment logic, and consistent formatting3. Quality, Process & Practice Support• Cross-check all output for arithmetic accuracy, formula integrity, and internal consistency before submitting for Manager review - zero-tolerance for avoidable errors• Maintain Qualicentric's template library and standardised workbooks; update templates based on engagement learnings and Manager direction• Prepare structured data request lists and manage follow-up with client finance teams under the engagement lead's oversight• Document analytical procedures and data sources clearly so work product can be reviewed, audited, or handed off without re-explanation• Participate in team knowledge-sharing sessions; actively build technical fluency in US GAAP standards relevant to both FP&A and FDD contextsWHAT YOU BRING• 3–8 years of experience in FP&A, financial analysis, or transaction advisory - Big-4, accounting firm, or corporate finance background preferred• CA / CPA / MBA (Finance) qualification required; strong academic record and analytical aptitude considered alongside formal credentials• Hands-on financial modelling skills in Excel - comfortable building models from scratch, not just populating existing templates; title: Legal Service Delivery Specialist, Global Frontline
description:
**Overview**
Microsoft’s Corporate, External & Legal Affairs (CELA) organization supports one of the most complex commercial businesses in the world. The Global Frontline team in Customer & Partner Solutions (CPS) serves as a legal front door for Microsoft Customer and Partner Solutions (MCAPS) and Microsoft Elevate, helping business clients obtain timely, practical legal support and resolving matters at the appropriate level while partnering with attorneys and subject matter experts on higher-risk or specialized issues.
  
  
The Legal Service Delivery Specialist is a frontline legal professional operating at the intersection of legal support, service delivery, and workflow improvement. You will serve as a primary legal contact for business clients, resolve complex matters within the team’s scope with minimal supervision, and work across CELA to identify risk, resolve issues, and deliver consistent support across regions.
  
  
This role offers the opportunity to help define the next generation of legal service delivery within CELA. In addition to supporting individual matters, you will help simplify recurring legal work, strengthen readiness, and develop more scalable ways to support the business. You will work with attorneys, legal professionals, and technology partners to improve workflows and responsibly use data, automation, and AI-enabled capabilities to increase the speed, quality, and reach of legal support.
  
  
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
  
  
**Responsibilities**
Frontline Legal Support and Client Counseling
  
  

* Serve as a primary legal contact for business clients and complex questions submitted through Global Frontline intake channels. Provide practical legal support with minimal supervision, identify issues and risks, and consult with attorneys or subject matter experts as appropriate.
* Draft, review, negotiate, and process legal and business materials and correspondence. Apply Microsoft policies and approved legal guidance to help clients move work forward while ensuring appropriate escalation and follow-through.
* Build strong knowledge of Microsoft’s businesses, commercial priorities, CELA processes, and relevant legal frameworks, and apply regional and cultural context to deliver practical, business-focused support.
* Manage a high volume of matters across multiple clients, priorities, and regions, exercising sound judgment regarding risk, prioritization, escalation, and resource allocation.

Service Delivery and Readiness
  
  

* Identify recurring client needs, readiness gaps, and process inefficiencies. Work with attorneys and other legal professionals to develop practical guidance, playbooks, intake requirements, training, and self-service resources that allow the team to take on work deliberately and consistently.
* Use service data and stakeholder feedback to identify trends, assess quality, and recommend improvements to Global Frontline’s scope, processes, and client experience.

Continuous Improvement and Workflow Innovation
  
  

* Help redesign repeatable legal work for scale and speed. Translate legal and business needs into improved workflows and partner with legal operations, technology, and engineering teams to implement solutions.
* Support responsible adoption of automation and AI-enabled capabilities in legal workflows, and lead or contribute to projects that help Global Frontline adopt more effective ways of working.

**Qualifications**
Required Qualifications
  
  

* Bachelor's Degree AND 5+ years experience in paralegal, legal administration, or relevant experience OR Paralegal Certification that meets the requirements for the location of work AND 6+ years experience in paralegal, legal administration, or relevant experience OR equivalent experience.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience supporting complex legal or compliance matters with limited supervision and exercising sound judgment regarding risk, prioritization, and escalation.
* Experience working directly with business clients and collaborating across legal, operational, or technical teams.
* Effective written and verbal communication skills.
* Experience in an in-house legal department, legal service provider, law firm, compliance function, or legal operations environment.
* Experience supporting a global organization or client population across regions and time zones.
* Experience improving legal processes or workflows and developing scalable legal resources.
* Experience using data, technology, automation, or AI-enabled tools to improve legal service delivery.

This position will be open for a minimum of 5 days, with applications accepted on an ongoing basis until the position is filled.

title: Direct Tax litigation Manager
description:
**JOB DESCRIPTION**

**1. Direct Tax Litigation Strategy & Dispute Resolution**

* Spearhead the organization’s end-to-end direct tax litigation strategy, providing final technical review and sign-off on high-stakes replies, appeals, written submissions, and paper books.
* Lead representation in critical and high-value matters before the Assessing Officer (AO), Dispute Resolution Panel (DRP), Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals) [CIT(A)], and the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT).
* Strategize, brief, and partner with external Senior Tax Counsels and Advocates for matters pending before the High Courts and the Supreme Court.
* Direct defense strategies for complex and sensitive proceedings, including Search & Seizure cases, Re-assessments (Section 147/148), Revision proceedings (Section 263/264), and penalty proceedings.
* Govern the central litigation management framework and tracker, ensuring strict adherence to statutory limitation periods and zero lapses in filing deadlines across the function.

**2. Regulatory Liaisoning & Assessment Oversight**

* Act as the senior point of contact and primary escalation interface with the Income Tax Department, building and maintaining constructive, high-trust relationships with senior tax authorities.
* Oversee the resolution of routine notices, scrutiny assessments, and faceless assessment proceedings under the Income Tax Act, 1961.
* Lead strategic engagements with the Investigation Wing, Transfer Pricing Officers (TPO), and Intelligence & Criminal Investigation (I&CI) divisions.
* Supervise and expedite high-priority post-assessment actions, including pending tax refunds, rectification applications (Section 154), and the release of seized assets or bank attachments.

**3. Strategic Tax Advisory & Risk Mitigation**

* Advise executive leadership on corporate tax planning, business restructuring, and complex direct tax matters to proactively minimize future litigation exposure.
* Evaluate the impact of new legislative amendments, CBDT circulars, and landmark judicial precedents on ongoing disputes and business operations, recalibrating litigation strategies accordingly.
* Partner with Finance, Accounting, and Audit leadership to ensure tax provisions, contingent liability evaluations, and tax audit disclosures align with strong, defensible legal positions.
* Lead litigation risk assessments during tax due diligence for proposed mergers, acquisitions, and strategic business transactions.

**4. Team Leadership & Capability Building**

* Lead, mentor, and manage a team of 5–6 direct tax professionals, overseeing day-to-day execution, bandwidth allocation, performance appraisals, and career progression.
* Review and refine legal research, pleadings, and submissions drafted by team members to ensure consistent technical quality and accuracy across all appellate forums.
* Drive continuous upskilling within the team through regular sessions on recent judicial rulings, procedural updates, and best practices in representation

title: Senior Compliance Manager
description:
**Company Description**

Dr. Reddy’s Laboratories Ltd. is a leading multinational pharmaceutical company based across global locations. Each of our 24,000 plus employees comes to work every day for one collective purpose: to accelerate access to affordable and innovative medicines because Good Health Can’t Wait.

We started in 1984 with a modest investment, 20 employees and a bold vision. Today, we have research and development centres, manufacturing facilities or a commercial presence in 66 countries.

For nearly four decades, we have stood for access, affordability and innovation based on the bedrock of deep science, progressive people practices and robust corporate governance. As the pharmaceutical industry evolves and undergoes disruption, we see an opportunity – to strengthen our core further (the next steps) and to build the future (the new bets).

‘The Next and the New’ is how we aim to continue to be the partner of choice – purpose-driven, future-ready and sustainable. Our aim is to reach over 1.5 Bn+ patients across the world by 2030 by growing our core businesses and building for the future with sustainability at the core of our purpose and strategy. Sustainability for us means operating in a manner that respects people, planet and purpose – helping us conserve precious resources, serve our patients, create value for stakeholders, give back to society, fulfil our potential and maintain our integrity and transparency

Dr Reddy’s maintains a work environment, free from discrimination and is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to employ & nurture all qualified diverse workforce without regard to race, colour religion, nationality, sex, age, disability status, genetics, sexual orientation, gender expression, citizenship or any other characteristic or classification protected by applicable law(s) of the country we operate in. We treasure every talent, and recognize merit and diversity in our organization.

**Job Description**

**Job Summary**

We are looking for an experienced Senior Business Compliance Manager for our Global Generics - India Sub-continent business. You will be involved in the creation, implementation, monitoring and effective compliance by the business stakeholders to key compliance polices as applicable to the marketing, promotional, sales and other commercial activities in GG India BU. This position will work closely with other compliance team members and support initiatives from various subject matter experts and stakeholders in the legal, finance departments.

**Roles & Responsibilities**

• You will be responsible for advising business stakeholders on carrying out business activities as per Dr Reddy's policies and the GG India SOPs and supporting other functions like Finance, HR etc in the same.

• You will be responsible for reviewing and approving marketing plans, HCP engagements and other material submitted to the compliance team's pre-clearance through m-Hub/LMRC and our ARF systems.

• You will be responsible for conducting in-depth root cause analysis, identification of processes and controls which are working and not working and suggesting corrective and preventive actions. You will also work alongside the Ombuds team in implementing their CAPAs and in upgrading processes and systems to prevent repetition of like issues in future

• You will be responsible for participating in the training, communication, and sensitization of the aspects of Code of Business Conduct and Ethics (COBE), GGI Marketing Code and other key compliance policies.

• You will be responsible for implementation of UCPMP/similar guidelines in the day-to-day conduct of business and preparing and presenting of key findings for senior management

**Qualifications**

Educational qualification: Lawyer or chartered accountant

Minimum work experience: 9-12 years in a compliance-related role, with a focus on policy writing, compliance advisory and CAPA management in pharmaceutical organisation.

**Additional Information**

**Technical Skills**

• Demonstrated understanding of the general pharmaceutical business, showcasing knowledge of industry dynamics, trends, and challenges.

• Strong proficiency in drafting policies & SOPs.

• Extensive experience in monitoring and in scrutiny of documents and records

• In-depth knowledge of relevant laws, regulations, and industry standards.

• Demonstrated expertise in compliance management and advising on pharma marketing and UCPMP.

• Proven track record in corporate compliance and implementing effective compliance programs.

**Behavioural skills**

• Strong written and oral communication abilities, facilitating effective expression of ideas.

• Demonstrates analytical thinking, enabling effective problem-solving and decision-making.

• Ability to multitask and manage a variety of business requirements simultaneously.

• Approaches tasks with a positive "can-do" attitude, demonstrating optimism and a solution-oriented mind set.

• Effective people management skills with colleagues and clients, fostering positive relationships.

• Competence in operating effectively within a diverse and complex matrix organization.

As consumers embrace new AI-driven experiences, the LiveRamp data collaboration network exponentially expands the breadth and accuracy of the data on which marketing AI capabilities operate, powering deeper customer insight and measurable performance on a global scale. LiveRamp is headquartered in San Francisco, California, with offices worldwide. Learn more at LiveRamp.com.
  
  
LiveRamp, Inc. is seeking a detail-oriented and proactive Contracts Manager to join our legal and procurement team. In this role, you will be responsible for managing, drafting, reviewing, and negotiating a wide variety of contracts to support business operations and mitigate risk. Your expertise will help streamline contract processes, ensure regulatory compliance, and foster effective relationships with internal stakeholders and external partners.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**

* Draft, review, negotiate, and manage a diverse array of contracts, including vendor agreements, customer contracts, NDAs, partnership agreements, and more.
* Advise teams across the organization on contract terms, obligations, risks, and best practices.
* Collaborate with legal counsel, finance, procurement, and other teams to ensure contracts align with company policies and business objectives.
* Maintain organized contract records and oversee the contract lifecycle to ensure timely renewals and compliance.
* Ensure all contracts adhere to company policies, regulatory requirements, and industry standards.
* Identify opportunities to improve and standardize contract processes and templates.

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree required; a degree in law, business administration, or a related field preferred.
* Proven experience as a Contracts Manager or in a similar role handling contract review, drafting, and negotiation.
* Strong analytical skills, with keen attention to detail and risk mitigation.
* Excellent communication and organizational skills.
* Ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines simultaneously in a fast-paced environment.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience working in the SaaS or technology sector.
* Familiarity with contract management software and workflow tools.
* Understanding of GDPR, CCPA, and data privacy regulations as they relate to contracts.

If you are a motivated contracts professional looking to make an impact at a dynamic, growing company, we invite you to apply!
  
  
We use automated decision systems (ADS) as part of our recruitment and hiring process. title: Commercial and Trademark Legal Counsel
description:
Your Team Responsibilities
  
  
On the forefront of the financial services industry, MSCI offers a fast-paced yet collegial environment, which is created through a strong culture of teamwork and close working relationships within the legal commercial contracts team and with other functional departments at MSCI. This is an excellent opportunity for an outstanding, highly motivated lawyer with experience in data and SaaS licensing and intellectual property, including trademarks, to work closely with our Commercial Legal teams in the Americas, EMEA and APAC. In addition to attending commercial legal team meetings, the role sits within a cutting-edge, AI-focused contract negotiation team operating across these regions.
  
  
Reporting and supervision: the role reports to Chris Harte, Head of AI Contract Team (based in London), with day-to-day functional leadership from Sonal Bane (based in Mumbai), partnering with MSCI's regional Commercial Legal teams and working with MSCI's Global IP Counsel on trademark matters.
  
  
Your Key Responsibilities
  
  

* Negotiate complex technology and data agreements to provide MSCI services, including data licenses, Software-as-a-Service arrangements, financial product licenses, managed services agreements, and redistribution arrangements primarily under New York law.
* Handle trademark matters in partnership with MSCI's IP team, including running trademark clearance knockout searches on proposed product, index and service names, providing a preliminary risk assessment, and recommending when a full search or outside counsel review is needed.
* Rapidly come up to speed on MSCI's AI capabilities, contracts, product offerings, risk tolerances, policies, and practices.
* Work collaboratively and creatively to design and implement new contract templates and provisions for new product offerings.
* Use and contribute to the development of MSCI's AI systems as an integral part of your work. No programming experience is necessary, but candidates should show self-directed adoption of new technology, i.e. tools they have taught themselves, processes they have changed or workarounds they have built, and ideally use of AI tools on live legal work.
* Work on any other legal projects, teams and assignments as they arise.

**Your Skills And Experience That Will Help You Excel**

* A total of 9+ years of experience and a minimum of 4 years experience in-house or at a premier law firm.
* Ability to carefully yet swiftly negotiate a high volume of complex agreements.
* Strong project management skills with the organizational capability to manage multiple deals and projects in a fast-paced environment.
* Experience negotiating complex tech and IP transactions.
* Experience with intellectual property matters, particularly trademarks, including conducting trademark clearance knockout searches and assessing likelihood-of-confusion risk. Familiarity with trademark search tools and registers (e.g., USPTO, TMView) is a plus.
* Entrepreneurial \"can do\" spirit and proactive desire to quickly learn the business and rapidly come up to speed in new areas.
* Positive, execution-oriented outlook, with superior listening skills, drafting ability and attention to detail.
* Strong communication skills and ability to build and maintain strong relationships with clients and colleagues.
* Law degree and license to practice.
* Experience in the financial services industry and/or working on M&A deals is helpful.

**About MSCI**
**What we offer you**

* Transparent compensation schemes and comprehensive employee benefits, tailored to your location, ensuring your financial security, health, and overall wellbeing.
* Flexible working arrangements, advanced technology, and collaborative workspaces.
* A culture of high performance and innovation where we experiment with new ideas and take responsibility for achieving results.
* A global network of talented colleagues, who inspire, support, and share their expertise to innovate and deliver for our clients.
* Global Orientation program to kickstart your journey, followed by access to our Learning@MSCI platform, AI Learning Center , LinkedIn Learning Pro and tailored learning opportunities for ongoing skills development.
* Multi-directional career paths that offer professional growth and development through new challenges, internal mobility and expanded roles.
* We actively nurture an environment that builds a sense of inclusion belonging and connection, including eight Employee Resource Groups. All Abilities, Asian Support Network, Black Leadership Network, Climate Action Network, Hola! MSCI, Pride & Allies, Women in Tech, and Women’s Leadership Forum.

At MSCI we are passionate about what we do, and we are inspired by our vision – to power better decisions. You’ll be part of an industry-leading network of creative, curious, and entrepreneurial pioneers. This is a space where you can challenge yourself, set new standards and perform beyond expectations for yourself, our clients, and our industry.
  
  
MSCI strengthens global markets by connecting participants across the financial ecosystem with a common language. Our research-based data, analytics and indexes, supported by advanced technology, set standards for global investors and help our clients understand risks and opportunities so they can make better decisions and unlock innovation. We serve asset managers and owners, private-market sponsors and investors, hedge funds, wealth managers, banks, insurers and corporates.

description:

This is a leadership role, responsible for building scalable legal processes, ensuring statutory and regulatory compliance, supporting fundraising and investor relations, and enabling business growth through strong governance and risk management.

· Manage day-to-day legal advisory and compliance requirements across the organization

· Establish and standardize legal frameworks, workflows, and internal controls

Hands-on experience building scalable legal processes and frame

title: Associate / Advocate
description:
**Company Description**

ELIXIR Legal Services is a premier law firm based in Mumbai, renowned for its exceptional legal expertise and client-centric approach. Our dedicated team of attorneys and legal advisors deliver tailored legal solutions to meet the specific needs of individuals and businesses. We represent clients in various courts, including district courts, high courts, and the Supreme Court of India. Our services include civil and criminal litigation, SRA/Redevelopment matters, dispute resolution, and bankruptcy proceedings. We cultivate a collaborative culture that emphasizes teamwork and mentorship, enabling our attorneys to tackle complex legal challenges confidently.

**Role Description**

This is a senior full-time, on-site position based in Mumbai for an Associate / Advocate with extensive experience in litigation before the Bombay High Court. The role involves independent handling of complex litigation matters, including strategy formulation, drafting, appearances, and client advisory. The candidate will be expected to lead proceedings, represent clients effectively before various courts and tribunals, and mentor junior team members. Key responsibilities include managing case portfolios, supervising drafting and research, coordinating with external counsels, and ensuring seamless client communication. The role also demands active participation in client strategy meetings, settlement negotiations, and internal knowledge-sharing initiatives that contribute to the firm’s overall excellence and growth.

**Qualifications**

* Minimum 15 years of demonstrated experience in litigation practice before the Bombay High Court.
* Strong command over civil, commercial, and procedural law, with proven ability to manage complex legal matters independently.
* Expertise in drafting pleadings, written submissions, and legal opinions with precision and clarity.
* Excellent oral advocacy and argumentation skills before courts and tribunals.
* Strong client advisory, negotiation, and relationship management capabilities.
* In-depth understanding of court procedures, filing processes, and regulatory compliance.
* LL.B. (or higher legal qualification) from a recognized institution and active membership with the Bar Council of India.
* Ability to lead teams, mentor junior advocates, and contribute to a culture of collaboration and professional growth.
* Experience in dispute resolution, redevelopment, and real estate matters will be considered an advantage.

title: Vice President Compliance
description:
**Job Title:**
Vice President/Senior Vice President – Compliance

**Company:**
Equentis Wealth Advisory Services Limited

**Department:**
Compliance

**Employment Type:**
Full-Time

**About the Company -**
Equentis Wealth Advisory Services Limited is a SEBI registered Investment Advisor, Portfolio Manager, Alternative Investment Fund and acts as distributor of third-party financial products. Equentis has more than 65000 subscribers in the investment advisory side and managing AUM of more than 150 crore in PMS and more than 200 crores under its AIF. The Company is in the process of further expansion by setting up offices in the GIFTCITY and in Dubai and obtaining Insurance Broking license.

**Job Overview**

Equentis is seeking an experienced professional who will act as Compliance Officer and Principal Officer and will lead the compliances related to
**Investment Advisory, Alternative Investment Fund, distribution business and Insurance Broking**
. The Primary Mandate of the role is to ensure strict adherence to the SEBI Act, applicable intermediary-specific regulations, PMLA guidelines, and circulars issued by SEBI, regulatory authorities.

The role will directly report to Chief Operation and Compliance Officer of the Equentis Group.

**Core Responsibilities**

**1. Regulatory Filings & Statutory Reporting**

* Manage timely submission of periodic returns, reports, documents to SEBI, BSE, IRDAI, AMFI, Trustees.
* Oversee registration renewals, prior-approval applications (change in control, shareholding, directors, or key management personnel), and intimations of material changes to Private Placement Memorandums (PPMs).
* Maintain statutory registers, Investment Advisory agreements, AIF contribution agreements, insurance solicitation records, and digital audit trails in accordance with prescribed retention norms.

**2. Surveillance & Internal Controls**

* **Client-Level Segregation (IA vs. Distribution):**
  Enforce strict separation between
  **Investment Advisory**
  and
  **Distribution/Execution**
  services at the client/family group level.
* **Chinese Walls & Conflict Management:**
  Maintain operational, physical, and IT barriers between Investment Advisory, AIF investment teams, and Insurance/MF Distribution units.
* **Product, Fee & Portfolio Controls:**
* *IA:*
  Audit client risk profiling, suitability rationale, and adherence to SEBI IA fee caps (AUA vs. Fixed Fee modes).
* *AIF:*
  Monitor adherence to PPM investment objectives, concentration limits, Sponsor/Manager continuing interest ("skin-in-the-game"), and independent valuation norms.
* *Insurance & Distribution:*
  Enforce adherence to IRDAI brokerage/reward limits, prevent rebating (Section 41 of the Insurance Act), and monitor AMFI ARN/EUIN compliance and SEBI Risk-o-meter rules.
* Keeping track of new circulars, assessing impact and implementing the changes across the organization.

**3. Policy Formulation, Marketing Approvals & Employee Training**

* Draft, update, and enforce internal Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), Code of Conduct, Chinese Wall policies, and such other compliance policies.
* Conduct mandatory periodic training and NISM certification tracking for employees and associated persons.
* Pre-Approve All Marketing & Pitch Material
  **:**
  Vet AIF pitchbooks, IA promotional content, insurance brochures, and social media posts against SEBI’s Advertisement Code (for IAs/AIFs) and IRDAI’s Insurance Advertisements.

**4. Audit Management & Inspection Readiness**

* Coordinate mandatory annual compliance audits for SEBI IA, annual AIF PPM audits and Compliance Test Reports (CTRs) to Trustees, IRDAI statutory/internal audits, and CSCRF (Cybersecurity & Cyber Resilience Framework) audits
* Manage regulatory inspections conducted by SEBI, BASL, IRDAI, or Trustees, track Audit Action Taken Reports (ATRs), and present consolidated compliance dashboards to the Board/Audit Committee

**5. Investor Grievance Redressal**

* Monitor complaints received through
  **SEBI SCORES**
  , the SMART ODR portal, and direct client channels.
* Ensure timely resolution within SEBI-mandated turnaround times and analyze root causes to prevent recurring service or compliance failures.

**6. Anti-Money Laundering (AML) & KYC Governance**

* Act as Principal Officer under PMLA.
* Oversee periodic KYC updates, CKYC/KRA uploads, and enhanced due diligence (EDD) for high-risk clients and Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs).

**Qualifications & Statutory Eligibility**

* **Education:**
  Company Secretary (ACS/FCS), Chartered Accountant (CA), LL.B., or MBA/Postgraduate in Finance or Law.
* **Mandatory Certifications:**
  Valid
  **NISM Series-III A**
  (Securities Intermediaries Compliance – Non-Fund) certification, plus intermediary-specific NISM certifications (e.g., NISM Certification for Investment Advisor, AIF).
* **Experience:**
  8–12 years in capital markets compliance, legal, or regulatory operations.
* **Fit & Proper Criteria:**
  Must meet SEBI’s "Fit and Proper Person" criteria under Schedule II of the SEBI (Intermediaries) Regulations, 2008, with a clean regulatory track record.

title: VP Special Situations & NCLT Acquisitions
description:
**Vice President – Special Situations & NCLT Acquisitions**
· Mumbai · Reports to the MD & CEO

**The mandate**

Our client is a large, listed Indian building-materials company with a brand several decades old, a national retail footprint and manufacturing in Gujarat. It is building a land and real-estate portfolio and plans to buy assets through the insolvency process under the IBC rather than in the open market. This role sets up that work and leads it. Done well, the Company will have a steady flow of distressed land and stalled projects that it has checked and priced, a team that can take a resolution plan from the EOI stage to NCLT approval, and its first deals closed on terms it can defend to its board.

**What you will own**

* **Deal origination:**
  Track CIRP and liquidation processes across NCLT benches, IBBI notices, Form G invitations and ARC/SARFAESI auctions, and keep a ranked pipeline of land and real-estate targets.
* **Diligence:**
  Personally lead title, legal, technical and financial diligence: 7/12 extracts, encumbrances, land-revenue records, RERA status, approvals, homebuyer liabilities and litigation. You will do this work yourself, not just send it to advisors.
* **Resolution plans:**
  Build and negotiate resolution plans, including valuation, waterfall, treatment of financial creditors, homebuyers and operational creditors, and the funding structure. Present them to Committees of Creditors (CoC) and Resolution Professionals.
* **Litigation and approvals:**
  Work with external counsel on Section 29A eligibility, objections, appeals before the NCLT and NCLAT, and the conditions attached to plan approval.
* **Post-acquisition handover:**
  Arrange the handover, clean up title, and transfer each asset to the development or monetisation team with a clear 100-day plan.
* **Governance:**
  Set up the investment committee process, approval thresholds and deal papers for the MD & CEO and the board.

**What you bring**

*Must have*

* 10–15 years' experience, with at least 5 in insolvency, stressed assets or special situations: at a stressed-asset fund, an ARC, a bank's stressed-assets team, a resolution-professional firm, or a developer that buys distressed assets.
* Personally closed at least two IBC resolution plans or liquidation acquisitions. The CV should name the deals and your role in each.
* Hands-on experience of real-estate title diligence in Maharashtra.
* Has negotiated directly with a CoC and with Resolution Professionals.
* CA, CFA, MBA (Finance) or LLB.

*Strongly preferred*

* Registered Insolvency Professional, or has worked closely with IBBI-registered professionals.
* Has worked on a stalled residential project where homebuyers were part of the creditor body.
* Knows the bankers, ARCs and RP firms active in Mumbai.

**What we look for beyond the CV**

* You do the work yourself. You read the title documents and build the model, and you don't only manage advisors.
* You are comfortable working directly with a promoter-style leadership team that decides quickly and expects you to own the outcome.
* You will walk away from a deal that doesn't make sense, and you can explain why in one page.
* You keep strict confidentiality around negotiations.

**Reporting and structure**

Reports to the MD & CEO. Leads a team of 3–5 people covering legal, finance and technical work. Works closely with group legal, finance, external counsel, valuers, and the land and development teams.

**Compensation**

Commensurate with experience.

title: Direct Tax litigation Manager
description:
**JOB DESCRIPTION**

**1. Direct Tax Litigation Strategy & Dispute Resolution**

* Spearhead the organization’s end-to-end direct tax litigation strategy, providing final technical review and sign-off on high-stakes replies, appeals, written submissions, and paper books.
* Lead representation in critical and high-value matters before the Assessing Officer (AO), Dispute Resolution Panel (DRP), Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals) [CIT(A)], and the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT).
* Strategize, brief, and partner with external Senior Tax Counsels and Advocates for matters pending before the High Courts and the Supreme Court.
* Direct defense strategies for complex and sensitive proceedings, including Search & Seizure cases, Re-assessments (Section 147/148), Revision proceedings (Section 263/264), and penalty proceedings.
* Govern the central litigation management framework and tracker, ensuring strict adherence to statutory limitation periods and zero lapses in filing deadlines across the function.

**2. Regulatory Liaisoning & Assessment Oversight**

* Act as the senior point of contact and primary escalation interface with the Income Tax Department, building and maintaining constructive, high-trust relationships with senior tax authorities.
* Oversee the resolution of routine notices, scrutiny assessments, and faceless assessment proceedings under the Income Tax Act, 1961.
* Lead strategic engagements with the Investigation Wing, Transfer Pricing Officers (TPO), and Intelligence & Criminal Investigation (I&CI) divisions.
* Supervise and expedite high-priority post-assessment actions, including pending tax refunds, rectification applications (Section 154), and the release of seized assets or bank attachments.

**3. Strategic Tax Advisory & Risk Mitigation**

* Advise executive leadership on corporate tax planning, business restructuring, and complex direct tax matters to proactively minimize future litigation exposure.
* Evaluate the impact of new legislative amendments, CBDT circulars, and landmark judicial precedents on ongoing disputes and business operations, recalibrating litigation strategies accordingly.
* Partner with Finance, Accounting, and Audit leadership to ensure tax provisions, contingent liability evaluations, and tax audit disclosures align with strong, defensible legal positions.
* Lead litigation risk assessments during tax due diligence for proposed mergers, acquisitions, and strategic business transactions.

**4. Team Leadership & Capability Building**

* Lead, mentor, and manage a team of 5–6 direct tax professionals, overseeing day-to-day execution, bandwidth allocation, performance appraisals, and career progression.
* Review and refine legal research, pleadings, and submissions drafted by team members to ensure consistent technical quality and accuracy across all appellate forums.
* Drive continuous upskilling within the team through regular sessions on recent judicial rulings, procedural updates, and best practices in representation

Pay: ₹35,000.00 - ₹45,000.00 per month

Work Location: In person

title: Company Secretary
description:
About the Company

Vardhman Electronics Private Limited is a rapidly growing multi-brand consumer electronics and home appliances retail company with an established presence across multiple states in India.

With a strong legacy spanning three decades, an extensive retail network and strategic associations with leading global and domestic brands, the Company continues to focus on sustainable business growth, operational excellence and the highest standards of corporate governance.

We are looking for a highly competent, experienced and proactive Company Secretary to independently lead and manage the Company's entire corporate secretarial and statutory compliance functions.

Role Overview

The ideal candidate should possess extensive practical knowledge of corporate laws, secretarial practices, statutory compliance and corporate governance.

The candidate will be responsible for ensuring comprehensive regulatory compliance, maintaining corporate records, managing statutory documentation and coordinating with internal departments, external professional agencies and regulatory authorities.

The role requires a high degree of ownership, professional competence, accuracy, integrity and confidentiality.

Key Roles & Responsibilities

**1. Corporate Secretarial & Statutory Compliance**

* Independently manage the entire corporate secretarial function of the Company.
* Ensure timely compliance with the Companies Act, 2013, and all other applicable laws, rules and regulations.
* Prepare and file statutory forms, annual returns and other regulatory submissions with the MCA, ROC and other statutory authorities.
* Maintain and regularly update statutory registers, records and corporate documents.
* Ensure compliance with applicable Secretarial Standards issued by ICSI.
* Handle matters relating to share capital, allotment, transfer, transmission and dematerialisation of shares.
* Develop and maintain a comprehensive statutory compliance calendar.
* Monitor statutory deadlines and ensure timely completion of all compliance requirements.

**2. Board Management & Corporate Governance**

* Organise and manage Board Meetings, Committee Meetings, Annual General Meetings and Extraordinary General Meetings.
* Prepare notices, agendas, explanatory statements, resolutions and minutes of meetings.
* Advise the Board of Directors and senior management on corporate governance and statutory matters.
* Formulate, review and implement corporate policies and governance frameworks.
* Manage documentation and compliance relating to directors, key managerial personnel and related-party transactions.
* Ensure proper constitution and functioning of Board-level committees, wherever applicable.
* Monitor implementation of decisions and resolutions passed by the Board and its committees.

**3. Corporate Documentation & Due Diligence**

* Independently manage the preparation, compilation, review and verification of corporate and statutory documentation.
* Coordinate with internal departments for the collection, validation and timely submission of information and supporting documents.
* Facilitate comprehensive corporate, legal and secretarial due diligence exercises.
* Review historical statutory records and identify compliance gaps, discrepancies and documentation deficiencies.
* Initiate and monitor necessary corrective and remedial actions.
* Ensure accuracy, completeness and consistency of corporate information across all statutory and regulatory documents.
* Establish and maintain a structured repository of corporate records and confidential documentation.
* Manage time-sensitive documentation assignments and ensure adherence to prescribed timelines.

**4. Coordination with External Professional Agencies**

* Act as the primary point of contact for external professional agencies, consultants, auditors, legal advisors and other stakeholders.
* Coordinate the preparation, review, finalisation and submission of documents required by external professional agencies.
* Ensure timely resolution of queries, observations and additional documentation requirements.
* Liaise with statutory and regulatory authorities on matters concerning the Company.
* Coordinate with statutory auditors, secretarial auditors and other professional advisors to facilitate smooth completion of their respective assignments.
* Monitor the progress of ongoing assignments and provide regular updates to senior management.

**5. Legal & Regulatory Compliance**

* Monitor changes in applicable corporate laws, rules and regulations and assess their implications for the Company.
* Review corporate agreements, declarations, undertakings and other legal and statutory documents.
* Identify potential regulatory and compliance risks and recommend appropriate corrective measures.
* Facilitate statutory audits, secretarial audits, compliance reviews and regulatory inspections, wherever applicable.
* Develop and strengthen internal compliance systems, processes and reporting mechanisms.
* Ensure strict confidentiality and appropriate handling of sensitive corporate information.

Educational Qualifications & Experience

* Qualified Company Secretary and an active member of the Institute of Company Secretaries of India (ICSI).
* 3–5 years of relevant post-qualification experience.
* Demonstrated experience in independently managing the complete secretarial function of an organisation.
* Strong practical knowledge of the Companies Act, 2013, Secretarial Standards and applicable corporate laws.
* Proven experience in handling complex corporate documentation, due diligence and regulatory compliance assignments.
* Experience in coordinating with multiple external professional agencies and managing time-bound assignments.
* Prior experience with large corporate organisations or established professional firms will be preferred.
* Additional qualifications such as LLB or LLM will be an added advantage.

Key Skills & Competencies

* Excellent drafting, analytical and documentation skills.
* Strong understanding of corporate laws and governance practices.
* Ability to work independently with minimal supervision.
* Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
* Strong organisational and time-management capabilities.
* Exceptional attention to detail and accuracy.
* Ability to manage multiple assignments under strict deadlines.
* High standards of professional integrity, discretion and confidentiality.
* Proactive, responsible and solution-oriented approach.

Why Join Us?

* Opportunity to independently lead the corporate secretarial function of a rapidly growing organisation.
* Direct interaction with the Board of Directors and senior management.
* Opportunity to contribute towards strengthening the Company's corporate governance and compliance framework.
* Professional, dynamic and growth-oriented working environment.
* Competitive remuneration commensurate with experience and professional capabilities.
* Long-term career growth opportunities.

How to Apply

Interested candidates possessing the requisite qualifications and relevant experience may apply through LinkedIn or share their updated CV at ayush@vardhmanelectronics.in

The Director, Contracts & Analysis leads the negotiation of commercial contract terms across a portfolio of client agreements and service lines, including results-based compensation (RBC) and other performance-linked constructs. The role partners with case teams, Legal, Finance and members of Bain's Consulting Leadership Team throughout the negotiation process and is accountable for the assessment and clear communication of issues, analysis and risks arising from proposed commercial terms.

It leads RBC governance and retrospective reviews of material programs, and drives updates to internal IP and best practice in step with global COE guidance.

  

**Principal Accountabilities**

**Contracting and negotiation**

* Lead negotiation of commercial contract terms across a portfolio of client agreements, working with Bain's client-facing, Legal and Finance teams to review proposals and draft contracts and provide guidance in support of client discussions
* Support Partners and the RCFO through the path to proposal and contracting stage, including commenting on pricing and proposal terms
* Proactively review existing contracts and amendments to identify open issues and address them with Partners to ensure timely renewals; partner with Office Heads to avoid expiration of rate cards
* Build and maintain the repeatable policies, templates and processes that govern contracting execution

  

**RBC construct support and governance**

* Partner with case teams and commercial leadership on RBC construct design and approval strategy, ensuring structures are consistent with internal guidelines, regional norms and all required approval dimensions
* Lead steerco preparation and facilitation for material live programs; maintain a governance cadence appropriate to program size and risk, and surface course-correction options early

**IP, process, systems and reporting**

* Develop metrics, dashboards and reports to monitor revenue cycle execution and provide insight for management planning; drive quality standards in execution
* Perform ad hoc analysis and activities as required for Finance and other internal and external stakeholders; consistently act in alignment with Bain's Operating Principles

  

**Qualifications:**

  

* Bachelor’s degree in Business, Accounting, Mathematics, Finance or Economics
* 10-15 years of progressive work experience in Finance roles including responsibility for providing senior management team support

title: Patent Associate
description:
**Company Description**
InventIP is a boutique intellectual property law firm specializing in IP strategy, IP audits, and the drafting, filing, and prosecution of patent, trademark, and design applications. Leveraging years of focused experience, the firm has built strong relationships with trusted attorneys worldwide, enabling efficient filing and prosecution across multiple jurisdictions. InventIP distinguishes itself through deep technical expertise and robust prosecution skills, contributing to a higher success rate in securing grants in various regions. The team has extensive experience working with multinational corporations, start-ups, SMEs, universities, research institutes, and individual inventors, offering tailored support across diverse innovation ecosystems.

This is a full-time, on-site Patent Associate role based in Delhi NCR. The Patent Associate will be responsible for drafting and reviewing patent specifications, preparing and filing patent applications, and managing prosecution before Indian and foreign patent offices. Day-to-day tasks include conducting prior art and patentability searches, analyzing technical disclosures, and collaborating with inventors and internal stakeholders to refine claims and strategy. The role also involves monitoring application timelines, responding to office actions, and supporting IP audits and portfolio management activities. The Patent Associate will work closely with senior attorneys to develop IP strategies that align with client business goals and protect key innovations.

**Qualifications**

* Strong skills in Patent Preparation and drafting clear, technically accurate patent specifications.
* Experience with Patent Applications, including filing, tracking, and coordinating prosecution across jurisdictions.
* Ability to conduct Patentability assessments and prior art searches, and to provide reasoned opinions on scope and validity.
* Solid understanding of Patent Law and procedures, with working knowledge of broader Intellectual Property concepts.
* Degree in engineering, science, or technology (e.g., electronics, computer science, mechanical, biotech) combined with a law or IP qualification preferred.
* Strong analytical, writing, and communication skills, with attention to detail and accuracy.
* Ability to collaborate with technical teams and inventors and to manage multiple matters and deadlines.
* Prior experience in an IP law firm or in-house IP department is an advantage.

title: Executive - GT Regulatory Capital Reporting
description:
Join our GT Regulatory Reporting Team in Group Finance and you will have an opportunity to work in a dynamic and collaborative environment. Our team is responsible for driving change across systems, ensuring optimal solution design for risk calculations.
  
  
We are a global financial services group operating in 30 markets with 57 years of unbroken profitability. At Macquarie, you’re empowered to shape a career that is fulfilling and creates value. You will bring your insights and expertise to the task at hand and feel supported as you make your own kind of impact for a better future.
  
  
**What role will you play?**
In this role, you will be responsible to run the capital/credit risk process to generate exposures for credit risk, counterparty credit risk, Risk weighted assets, Leverage ratio, Large exposures, regulatory Returns, Pillar 3 disclosures based on the guidance issued by regulators and performing UATs for all regulatory & system driven changes. Additionally, you will play a pivotal role in creating & running the controls over the reporting processes and ensuring that control design is in line with Macquarie’s control framework and complies with all requirements. You will also contribute in responding to internal and external audit queries and adhoc requests and queries from the regulators.
  
  
**What You Offer**

* CA with 1.5-2.5 years of post-qualification experience or MBA Finance (or equivalent post graduate) with 2.5-4 years of post-qualification experience in the financial services industry.
* Knowledge of regulatory reporting requirements / developments, fundamental of accounting and consolidation. Previous experience in a Regulatory Reporting role is added advantage
* Knowledge on financial instruments and products offered by investment banks
* Strong interpersonal and communication skills. Self-motivated and capable of working in a team environment
* Good analytical ability. Ability to work under pressure, report to tight deadlines and deal effectively with issues

We love hearing from anyone inspired to build a better future with us, if you're excited about the role or working at Macquarie we encourage you to apply.
  
  
**What We Offer**
**Benefits**
At Macquarie, you’re empowered to shape a career that’s rewarding in all the ways that matter most to you. Macquarie employees can access a wide range of benefits which, depending on eligibility criteria, include:
  
  

* 1 wellbeing leave day per year
* 26 weeks’ paid maternity leave or 20 weeks’ paid parental leave for primary caregivers along with 12 days of paid transition leave upon return to work and 6 weeks’ paid leave for secondary caregivers
* Company-subsidised childcare services
* 2 days of paid volunteer leave and donation matching
* Benefits to support your physical, mental and financial wellbeing including comprehensive medical and life insurance cover, the option to join parental medical insurance plan and virtual medical consultations extended to family members
* Access to our Employee Assistance Program, a robust behavioural health network with counselling and coaching services
* Access to a wide range of learning and development opportunities, including reimbursement for professional membership or subscription
* Hybrid and flexible working arrangements, dependent on role
* Reimbursement for work from home equipment

Financial Management, People and Engagement (FPE) provides a single interface for Macquarie’s businesses across key areas of people, strategy, communications and financial management. Comprising two pillars – Financial Management, and People and Engagement – it is responsible for managing the Group’s financial, tax and treasury activities and strategic priorities, fostering our culture through people and community engagement strategies, and engaging with stakeholders to protect and promote Macquarie’s reputation globally.

Macquarie provides access to opportunities for all individuals regardless of race, colour, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, protected veteran status, genetic information, marital status, gender identity or any other characteristic or circumstance.

title: Senior Associate (Corporate, Funds & Regulatory)
description:
**Job Title:**
Senior Associate (Corporate, Funds & Regulatory)

**Organisation:**
Lex Mores LLP

**Location:**
Greater Noida West (On-site – 5 Days Working)

**Experience:**
5–7 years PQE

**Employment Type:**
Full-time

**Joining:**
Immediate Joiners Preferred

**Practice Area:**
Corporate & Commercial Law, Investment Funds, SEBI Regulatory Advisory and Intellectual Property

**1. Role Overview**

**We are looking for an experienced corporate lawyer with strong expertise in Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs), SEBI regulations, investment transactions, commercial contracts and intellectual property agreements.**

**The candidate should possess strong legal and commercial acumen, be capable of independently handling complex legal assignments, advising clients, identifying regulatory and commercial risks, and delivering practical, business-oriented legal solutions.**

**The role requires someone who goes beyond legal drafting and understands the commercial intent, regulatory implications and long-term interests of clients.**

**2. Key Roles and Responsibilities**

**A. Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) & SEBI Regulatory Advisory**

* Advise clients on the structuring, establishment, registration and operations of Category I, II and III AIFs.
* Interpret and advise on SEBI (Alternative Investment Funds) Regulations, 2012, applicable circulars and regulatory developments.
* Draft, review and negotiate Private Placement Memorandums (PPMs), Contribution Agreements, Investment Management Agreements, Trust Deeds and other fund-related documents.
* Advise on the roles, responsibilities and fiduciary obligations of Sponsors, Fund Managers, Trustees and Investment Committees.
* Advise on regulatory compliance, governance structures, conflicts of interest and related-party transactions.
* Conduct regulatory due diligence and compliance audits.
* Prepare detailed legal opinions on complex SEBI and securities law matters.
* Advise on regulatory implications of fund-related communications, marketing, promotions and third-party associations.

**B. Corporate Transactions & Investment Agreements**

* Draft, review and negotiate:
* Share Subscription Agreements (SSA)
* Shareholders' Agreements (SHA)
* Share Purchase Agreements (SPA)
* Investment Agreements
* Term Sheets
* Joint Venture Agreements
* Founders' Agreements
* Convertible Instrument Agreements
* ESOP Schemes
* Handle legal due diligence for investments, acquisitions and corporate restructuring.
* Advise on shareholder rights, investor protection, exit mechanisms, governance and transaction structuring.
* Advise on applicable provisions of the Companies Act, FEMA and RBI regulations.

**C. Commercial Contracts**

* Independently draft, review and negotiate complex commercial agreements, including technology, SaaS, licensing, service, vendor, distribution, outsourcing and strategic collaboration agreements.
* Understand clients' business models and translate commercial arrangements into legally enforceable agreements.
* Identify legal and commercial risks and recommend appropriate mitigation mechanisms.
* Participate in contract negotiations and advise clients on alternative contractual positions.
* Develop customised contractual frameworks aligned with clients' business objectives.

**D. Intellectual Property & Technology Agreements**

* Draft and negotiate IP Assignment Agreements, Licensing Agreements, Technology Transfer Agreements, Software Development Agreements and IP Collaboration Agreements.
* Advise on intellectual property ownership, commercialisation, licensing and protection.
* Advise on protection of proprietary technology, trade secrets, business know-how and confidential information.
* Identify and mitigate IP-related risks arising from commercial and investment transactions.

**E. Client Advisory & Legal Research**

* Independently conduct client consultations and understand complex business requirements.
* Undertake detailed legal research and statutory interpretation.
* Prepare well-reasoned legal opinions, advisory notes and risk assessment reports.
* Provide practical recommendations rather than merely identifying legal issues.
* Stay updated on regulatory and legislative developments relevant to clients.

**F. Team Management & Quality Assurance**

* Review and supervise legal work undertaken by junior associates.
* Ensure legal accuracy, drafting quality, attention to detail and timely delivery.
* Mentor junior lawyers and develop their legal and commercial understanding.
* Take end-to-end ownership of client assignments.
* Establish and maintain high standards of legal service delivery.

**3. Mandatory Qualifications & Experience**

* LL.B. or integrated law degree from a recognised university.
* 5–7 years of post-qualification experience in corporate and commercial law.
* Demonstrable hands-on experience in AIF-related assignments and SEBI regulatory advisory.
* Prior experience in drafting and negotiating SSA, SHA and other investment transaction documents.
* Strong experience in complex commercial contract drafting and negotiations.
* Experience in intellectual property and technology-related agreements.
* Strong understanding of corporate laws, securities laws and applicable regulatory frameworks.
* Excellent legal research, drafting and communication skills.

**Additional Role Requirements & How to Apply**

* **Work Schedule & Location:**
  5 days working, reporting daily to our Greater Noida West office.
* **Communication:**
  Strong proficiency in written and spoken English.
* **Availability:**
  Immediate joiners are preferred.
* **How to Apply:**
  Apply directly here on
  **LinkedIn**
  or send your updated CV to
  **hr@contractbazaar.in**
  with your name and role in the subject line.

* Sector experience in Information Technology.
* Prior experience in an in-house legal environment preferably with a multinational company.
